The directorate of revenue intelligence, DRI, has dismantled a major network involved in importing Southeast Asian Arikanaths into India by falsely declaring them as being of Bangladeshi origin and fraudulently availing concessional duty benefits under the South Asian free trade area SAFTA.
The finance minister said the investigation has so far revealed a potential revenue loss of more than 2500 crore rupees, nine persons have been arrested in connection with the case.
Import of Arikanaths into India attracts a basic customs duty of 100%.
However, eligible imports under the SAFTA agreement are exempt from customs duty.
We have more from our correspondent.
The DRI said intelligence gathered during the investigation indicated that certain syndicates were fraudulently claiming SAFTA benefits on a large scale.

The syndicates were importing Arikanaths originating from Indonesia, Thailand, Malaysia and other Southeast Asian countries but declaring their country of origin as Bangladesh while importing them into India.
Based on intelligence inputs, the DRI conducted simultaneous searches at multiple premises linked to importers, customs brokers and IEC holders in Kolkata and Vishakhapatnam.
Several incriminating documents and other evidence establishing the Southeast Asian origin of the Arikanaths were recovered.
The investigation is continuing to identify other members of the syndicate and determine the full extent of the revenue loss.
